interface.name: interceptor_background_pointer_v1
interface.description: Compositor integration for qualified native Wayland targets. Caller and target connection peers must share the compositor's retained user/login identity. A lost or ambiguous login revokes the loaded integration. Commands contain bounded numeric target/point fields and a named input operation. They cannot contain arbitrary code or launch a process. A result describes delivery. Application effects require observation. Version 2 adds menu-guard. Version 1 clients retain pointer delivery. The menu-guard operation borrows a target-scoped popup guard for at most 750 milliseconds, until its resource is destroyed or login is revoked. Its zero-delivery acknowledgement does not invoke any menu or input. Version 3 adds typed app lifecycle requests. The process fd pins the selected kernel process. Every target connection must authenticate against that handle and the retained graphical login before mutation. Hide, unhide and quit preserve focus. Activate explicitly changes it. Version 4 adds launch-guard followed by a 64-character lowercase hex token. It creates no process and delivers no input. For ten seconds, matching native windows from the same authenticated login open floating to preserve existing layout, and suppress initial focus and application activation. Floating placement remains after the scope ends. At most 64 windows belong to one connection-owned guard. Expiry, disconnect and unload restore only the saved window flags. Earlier versions refuse before process launch.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: nonzero request id, never reused on this object

arg.name: command
arg.summary: bounded named operation and numeric fields

arg.name: success
arg.summary: one when delivery or a zero-delivery menu guard completed

arg.name: process_fd
arg.summary: retained live Linux PIDfd for the selected process
